source: AIDOC-catalogued Khmer farmer leaflet, "Coconut Cultivation Techniques for Farmers", prepared with NGO partners including Santi Sena, Buddhism for Development, and a farmer/agriculture association
text:
Nursery bed site selection: choose a clean site close to a reliable water source, with well-drained ground (not prone to waterlogging) and fertile soil suited to germination.

Nursery method: carefully split/trim the husk around the germination-pore end of each selected seed nut, without removing all of the husk, so the nut still has support and stored moisture during germination. Bury the nuts close together in rows in the nursery bed so they can be watered and monitored easily as a batch. The leaflet's illustration shows a farmer trimming husks with a knife over a low stand, with the trimmed nuts then laid in parallel rows in the nursery bed, germination-pore end up, ready to sprout. Seedlings are grown on in the nursery bed and monitored until they reach transplanting size (the leaflet's later section on transplanting refers to seedlings of roughly one year old as the target transplant stage).
